> OutBound is a compact, handheld ESP32-S3 powered cyberdeck featuring an ILI9341 TFT display, MAX7219 LED matrix, I2S audio output, and a custom 3D-printed enclosure. It functions as a portable wireless command terminal utilizing ESP-NOW communication, tactile buttons, and an integrated rechargeable power supply circuit.

## Design

### 2026-11-07: Started working on the main interface for the OutBound cyberdeck during this session.

**4.5h**

Started working on the main interface for the OutBound cyberdeck during this session.

### What I Worked On:
* **ILI9341 Screen Setup:** Focused on initializing the 2.4-inch display layout and testing basic text and element rendering on the screen.
* **Navigation Inputs:** Connected and mapped the push buttons (SW2 on GPIO2) to start building out a simple menu navigation system.

### What Worked & Challenges:
* Screen initialization went smoothly over SPI.
* Spending time getting the interface coordinate layout and menu spacing to look clean on the screen took most of the session.

### What's Next:
* Refining the UI layout, polishing the menu options, and hooking up screen actions to the hardware buttons and making "apps" to use.

### 2026-11-07: Session Objective

**4h**

Session Objective
Focus on hardening the core application suite (Music, Camera, and Photos), integrating a dedicated physical hardware Home button for universal navigation, and completely resolving UI flicker for a fluid, professional operating system feel.

Key Accomplishments & Implementation Details
1. Application Suite Polish (Music, Camera, & Photos)
Music App: Finalized the Spotify-inspired dark UI (#181818 background with #1CED60 accents), integrating dynamic track title rendering, geometric vector play (▶) and pause (⏸) indicators, and real-time progress bar scrubbing via the rotary encoder roll.

Camera App: Built out the tactical viewfinder layout complete with adjustable zoom levels (1.0x to 5.0x) via encoder rotation, an on-screen white flash snapshot effect for photo capture, and a live toggling video recording timer ([ ● REC ]).

Photos App: Styled a clean warm-white and cream gallery interface (#FFFCF5) displaying placeholder SD card image slots (IMG_001.JPG to IMG_003.JPG), complete with a safety-first double-press delete confirmation prompt ("PRESS SKIP BUTTON AGAIN TO CONFIRM").

2. Hardware Architecture & Home Button Integration
Dedicated Home / Back Button (GPIO 8): Wired a physical tactile switch to GPIO 8, creating an absolute hardware shortcut. Pressing this button from any active app state immediately aborts execution and snaps the display back to the main system menu.

Input Separation: Locked down the control schema so that the rotary encoder is reserved exclusively for rolling/navigating/scrubbing/zooming, while all primary selections and app triggers are cleanly mapped to the dedicated Select button on Pin 2.

3. UI Rendering & Flicker Elimination
Smart Incremental Redrawing: Diagnosed and resolved the visual flashing issue caused by full-screen clearing (tft.fillScreen) during encoder rotation.

Performance Gain: Replaced heavy screen wipes in the system menu with targeted coordinate-based rectangle clearing (updateMenuCursor). This ensures that rotating the encoder only updates the active and previous text lines, resulting in instantaneous, jitter-free menu navigation and a polished, consumer-grade user experience.

### 2026-11-07: Session Objective

**2h**

Session Objective
Develop and integrate a fully playable, retro-style Dino Run mini-game into the OutBound OS games suite, mapping custom arcade mechanics directly to the hardware button layout (Pin 2 for Jump, Pin 3 for Duck, and Rotary Encoder for menu selection).

Key Technical Implementation Details
1. Input Mapping & Control Scheme
Menu Navigation: Utilized the rotary encoder roll (GPIO 4 & 5) to select "Dino Run" from the games submenu with zero-flicker incremental row redrawing.

Jump Action (Pin 2): Wired a tactile button to Pin 2, triggering an instantaneous upward velocity vector (dinoVy = -11) when pressed, provided the player is grounded. Also doubles as the restart trigger upon a Game Over state.

Duck Action (Pin 3): Wired a secondary tactile button to Pin 3. Holding Pin 3 dynamically shrinks the dinosaur's hitbox and switches rendering bounds to a lower profile (isDucking = true), allowing clearance under obstacles.

2. Game Physics & Engine Loop
Gravity & Vertical Mechanics: Implemented a real-time physics tick (~30ms loop) where gravity (+1 acceleration per frame) pulls the player back down until they land squarely on the ground coordinate (dinoY = 165).

Obstacle Spawning & Movement: Procedurally scrolls cactus obstacles from right to left across the display. Successfully passing an obstacle increments the persistent score counter (+10 points).

Collision Detection: Built bounding-box collision logic checking dynamic dinosaur dimensions (standing vs. ducking height) against incoming obstacle coordinates, instantly transitioning the app state to the Game Over screen upon impact.

3. UI & Display Rendering
Dark Arcade Theme: Designed a clean, high-contrast arcade aesthetic utilizing dark blue backgrounds (#14141E), a crisp white ground line, cyan player sprites, and red obstacle markers on the ILI9341 display.

HUD Overlay: Integrated real-time score tracking in the top right corner and clear footer prompt instructions (Pin 2: Jump | Pin 3: Duck | Home: Menu).

### 2026-11-07: Session Objective

**3h**

Session Objective
Develop, integrate, and fine-tune the second arcade title, Space Runner, into the OutBound OS games submenu. The design focuses on responsive arcade controls utilizing Pin 3 for lateral movement with corner wrap-around and Pin 2 for laser combat.

Key Technical Implementation Details
1. Advanced Control Scheme & Corner Wrap-Around
Lateral Movement (Pin 3): Wired to a tactile button on Pin 3. Each press shifts the player's starfighter right (+16px). To optimize gameplay on compact cyberdeck screens, corner wrap-around logic was implemented: when the ship exceeds the right boundary (playerShipX > 290), its position automatically wraps around to the far left corner (playerShipX = 15), enabling continuous tactical dodging without dead ends.

Laser Combat & Restart (Pin 2): Mapped to Pin 2, serving a dual purpose: firing laser projectiles during active gameplay and acting as the quick-restart trigger on the Game Over screen.

2. Game Mechanics & Projectile Physics
Enemy Spawning & Descent: Procedurally generates hostile enemy craft descending vertically from the top of the screen at a steady game-tick rate (~35ms loop). If an enemy breaches the bottom boundary without being intercepted, the player loses a life (spaceLives--).

Laser Projectile Engine: Pressing Pin 2 spawns an active laser bolt directly above the starfighter's current X coordinate, moving upward rapidly (bulletY -= 10).

Collision Detection: Implemented precise bounding-box hit-detection checking whether active laser coordinates intersect with enemy sprite bounds. A successful hit awards score points (+20) and clears the enemy for a new spawn, while dropping lives to zero triggers the Game Over state.

3. UI & Aesthetic Design
Retro Sci-Fi Theme: Styled with a deep space-dark background palette (#0A0A14), neon pink headers, cyan laser bursts, green starfighter sprites, and high-visibility red enemy markers.

HUD & Status Overlay: Displays real-time score tracking (SCR) and remaining lives (LIV) in the top right corner, backed by clear footer prompt instructions (Pin 3: Move Right (Wrap) | Pin 2: Shoot).

### 2026-11-07: In this final polish pass, the visual enhancements extended far beyond a single mini-game, elevating the entire OutBound OS. Every interface—from the cream-colored system menu and Spotify-inspired mus

**2.5h**

In this final polish pass, the visual enhancements extended far beyond a single mini-game, elevating the entire OutBound OS. Every interface—from the cream-colored system menu and Spotify-inspired music player to the tactical camera view, photo gallery, and arcade suite—was refined with consistent spacing, crisp typography, and optimized incremental redrawing. This global visual upgrade unifies the cyberdeck experience into a cohesive, professional-grade operating system.
